reasons.A: Correct no-code/free forms concept, but assumes volume-based paid upgrade despite supplied unlimited-free forms/submissions. Paid-plan conditions and trials are not established by evidence.
reasons.B: Three distinct broad groups, but no narrow first-workflow timing trigger. Describes freelancers as highly motivated and access as ready without research; willingness to pay is particularly weak for a free offering.
reasons.C: Self-service label does not translate into product-led strategy. Cold email, LinkedIn InMail and bidding on design jobs are outbound variants, not a useful comparison against templates/use-case distribution. Public profiles do not establish available email access or free InMail/bids.
reasons.D: Ten emails in two hours is bounded, but prospect permissions/access, personalisation and activation steps are underdeveloped. Adjust after ten, stop after twenty and switch channels on silence without diagnosing access. Two interested replies is an arbitrary success threshold.
reasons.E: Free activation versus actual payment is not operationally separated. Volume-upgrade monetisation conflicts with the supplied free/unlimited proposition, and interest/trial requests are used as success.
reasons.F: First-buyer sentence is unfinished. The initial message invents a positive observation about the recipient's work; no verified-research placeholder. Conditional channels can add unacknowledged costs.
